controls_matched: A/B/D identical token multiset, length, template, and position tags; content-masked renders are byte-identical across arms
description: position-tagged opaque ordered varṇa IDs, e.g. 'p1:U25 p2:U17 p3:U19 p4:U27'
evaluator_receives: position-tagged opaque ID sequences for arms of a single hidden word
positive_result_supports: that ordered opaque varṇa composition is a recoverable, distinguishable STRUCTURAL signal — order is preserved and usable, not collapsed
primary_contrast: WITHIN-word A (true order) vs B (order-scramble); A vs D (unordered) secondary

rejected_alternatives.cross_word_candidate_match (Model 2): leaks via unique first unit + distinct inventories -> tests inventory
rejected_alternatives.learned_key (Model 1): needs a training phase not yet designed; deferred
rejected_alternatives.semantic_glosses (Option C / Model 4): reintroduces B1.10 prose-packet confound; secondary only

target_answer: a structural order judgment (e.g. which arm is the reference's true order / whether two renders share the same order) — NOT a word or meaning
why_inventory_alone_insufficient: within a trial all arms share the exact multiset and length, so inventory/length carry zero discriminative information
why_true_order_could_help: A differs from B and D only in the ORDER of an identical multiset; any above-chance discrimination must use order, since inventory+length are held constant
